title: DMT Experience: How to Go About it, and What to Expect
abstract:
### Microdosing  
[Microdosing](https://doubleblindmag.com/microdosing/what-you-should-know-about-microdosing-for-anxiety/), if you’re not familiar, is the act of taking an amount of a psychoactive substance that is too small to yield any notable intoxication. Cannabis, LSD, and psilocybin mushrooms are all commonly microdosed. The reasons why people microdose can vary: Maybe they’re looking to open up their creativity a bit, or soothe their social anxiety. Either way, the aim is to get the desired effects without getting high. And you can microdose DMT as well.  
While microdosing DMT doesn’t have the same afterglow potential as a full DMT experience, it still appears to have some soothing effects. A University of California Davis [study](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acschemneuro.8b00692) from 2019 found that rats which had received ultra-low does of DMT were less susceptible to fear and depression-like behaviours than their counterparts in the control group.
[Microdosing DMT](https://thethirdwave.co/microdosing/dmt/) isn’t difficult, but it will take a bit of careful planning. The idea is to take a very small amount of DMT every few days for as long as you want to continue to reap the benefits of doing so. While we already mentioned that taking just a small amount of DMT will prevent you from experiencing any intoxicating effects, figuring out exactly how much that “small amount” is can take time to figure out. As with any potentially intoxicating substance, start low and go slow is the rule.
## Therapeutic DMT Experiences  
We’ve mentioned briefly that DMT experiences can be deeply therapeutic. Ayahuasca ceremonies in particular have helped people overcome complex emotions like [grief](https://doubleblindmag.com/ayahuasca-heal-grief-iceers/) and mental health challenges such as [eating disorders](https://doubleblindmag.com/can-psychedelics-treat-eating-disorders/). Other people use their DMT experiences to fight [chronic pain](https://doubleblindmag.com/can-psychedelics-treat-physical-illness/), and a Canadian startup has been exploring the use of DMT experiences in [addiction treatment](https://doubleblindmag.com/entheon-dmt-addiction/).  
*Read: [Rick Strassman on DMT and the Mystical State](https://doubleblindmag.com/rick-strassman-dmt-mystical-state/)*  
In fact, DMT is an [endogenous substance](https://doubleblindmag.com/why-does-the-brain-make-its-own-dmt/), meaning it is naturally produced within the human body. While we’re not quite sure yet why our bodies make DMT, there is some suggestion that things like [orgasms](https://doubleblindmag.com/do-orgasms-cause-the-release-of-dmt/) and the phenomenon of near-death experiences are a tiny DMT experience of their own.
